entries.title: Genesis 42:1
segments: Look upon one another; in perplexity and despair.

entries.title: Genesis 42:2
segments: In seasons of danger and distress nothing is gained by despondency. The question should be, What shall we do? and having ascertained, we should, without delay, and in dependence on God, attempt to do it.  He helps those who, in the right way, attempt to help themselves.

entries.title: Genesis 42:6
segments:
That sold; directed as to the selling. 
 
  Bowed down;

entries.title: Genesis 42:7
segments: Made himself strange; acted as one that did not know them.

entries.title: Genesis 42:9
segments:
The nakedness of the land; its defenceless points, where and how a successful attack might be made upon it. 
 
The efforts of men to thwart the plans of God are the means of fulfilling them; yet they are as wicked in opposing him, as if he did not make what they do the occasion of promoting his cause.

entries.title: Genesis 42:14
segments: That is it that I spake unto you;what I said to you before,

entries.title: Genesis 42:15
segments: By the life of Pharaoh; as surely as Pharaoh lives.

entries.title: Genesis 42:16
segments: Men are often strongly tempted to do evil that good may come, but it is never right; and the success of a plan is no sure evidence of the righteousness of the means used in prosecuting it.

entries.title: Genesis 42:17
segments:
Ward; prison. 
 
  Three days; this gave them time to reflect upon their past conduct, their treatment of Joseph and Jacob, and upon their present condition and prospects.  This was what Joseph intended, and he no doubt prayed that it might be for their good.

entries.title: Genesis 42:20
segments: Be verified; be proved to be true.

entries.title: Genesis 42:21
segments:
Guilty concerning our brother; conscience condemned them for their treatment of Joseph, more than twenty years before. 
 
  Therefore is this distress; they viewed it as a punishment of their sins.

entries.title: Genesis 42:28
segments:
They were afraid; lest they should be charged with having stolen the money, and by treated as thieves. 
 
  God hath done; in his providence caused to come upon us as a punishment for our sin. 
 
When men have done what they know to be wicked, and evils come upon them, conscience links the two together, and views the one as a punishment for the other.

entries.title: Genesis 42:37
segments: Slay my two sons; that is, you may slay them, if I bring not Benjamin back again; a rash expression, but it showed Reuben's earnestness and sincerity.

entries.title: Genesis 42:38
segments: His brother; that is, Joseph; his own brother by Rachel.
